A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWAT research work. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete supplements are readable and support reliable matching despite the revised title, layout, and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original SWAT and finetuning experiments on five datasets, with component ablations, retrieval-size experiments, and classifier-retraining analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments on nine datasets, including additional retrieval-ranking, filtering, and augmentation results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The core two-stage SWAT procedure, cross-entropy objective, and classifier retraining remain unchanged. V2 adds CutMix-augmented few-shot finetuning alongside the original variant and explicitly evaluates filtered-SWAT variants (Tables 7–10). These are limited procedural extensions; the renamed method and expanded retrieval description alone do not establish a redesign.

E1.justification: V2 retains Semi-Aves, Flowers, Aircraft, EuroSAT, and DTD, and adds OxfordPets, Food101, StanfordCars, and ImageNet to actual evaluation. This substantially broadens recognition coverage to pets, food, cars, and large-scale object classification. ImageNet was explicitly excluded in v1.

E2.justification: V1 Table 14's comparison using mixed retrieved and few-shot training data disappears, removing WiSE-FT, FLYP, plain linear probing, and the mixed-data CrossModal-LP and REAL-Linear comparisons. Their appearances in other settings do not preserve this comparison. V2 also adds retrieval-ranking alternatives and CutMix-strict, while retaining the principal benchmark comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported optimizer from Adam to AdamW; this does not establish whether experiments were rerun. V2 adds a 10-epoch ImageNet budget and validation-set testing, explicit ranking/filtering controls, and a 10-image retrieval cap while dropping the 2,000-image cap. Retrieved pools also change substantially: DTD at cap 500 increases from 4,871 to 23,364 images in Table 16.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled retrieval-ranking and filtering studies, CutMix-strict and few-shot-only CutMix ablations, and visual case studies of DTD mismatch and rejected noisy images. The retrieval-size analysis now investigates very small retrieved sets. Existing initialization, common/rare-class, and retraining-duration analyses are retained and extended, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report averaged accuracy, with standard deviations in Table 3 and retraining plots. V2 expands results and redraws uncertainty displays without introducing a different statistical reporting practice or an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark, filtering, ranking, and augmentation results and removes the finetuning-comparison results. Table 2's 16-shot SWAT mean changes from 77.8 to 78.2 across different dataset sets, so this is not a same-setting gain. DTD's default result changes from 71.6 in v1 Table 8 to 66.3 in v2 Table 7; 71.6 reappears for v2's T2I-filtered variant in Table 10.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The empirical rare-class definition and existing mathematical descriptions are retained; v2 adds no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain full visual-encoder finetuning and two-stage retrieval-augmented learning for few-shot recognition. The advertised advantage changes from approximately 10% on five benchmarks to approximately 6% on nine. The abstract also changes retrieved-only finetuning from barely surpassing state-of-the-art zero-shot methods to underperforming them, reflecting revised evaluation rather than a matched-setting reversal.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies applicability by discussing default SWAT's failures against CLAP on DTD and Cars and interpreting filtering benefits through reduced noise and improved balance. It explicitly explains why base-to-novel evaluation is outside scope and adds the limitation that imbalance and domain-gap effects remain to be disentangled. The central mechanism explanations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation: synonym matching, T2T ranking and filtering thresholds, temperature optimization details, baseline settings, and a code-instructions section specifying Python/PyTorch versions, packages, resources, licensing, and reproduction guides. V1 already supplied core hyperparameters and the repository link, so code availability itself is not newly established. The dataset-license column is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for the four additional datasets and Madan et al. for its annotation motivation and evaluation critique. It removes several human-in-the-loop/annotation references, the FLYP citation, and the reference supporting ImageNet exclusion. The principal positioning relative to VLM adaptation, retrieval augmentation, and long-tailed learning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, and discussion are extensively rewritten. V2 separates problem and evaluation setup, adds explicit remarks on evaluation scope, and reorganizes the supplement from Sections A–G into A–I. The paper title and SWAT expansion also change. This is pervasive narrative revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 converts the document to two-column layout, exchanges the order of the overview and headline-results figures, and restructures detailed tables around shot groups and nine dataset columns. It adds retrieval/filtering tables and DTD/noisy-image panels, expands benchmark plots, and removes the earlier finetuning-comparison table. Existing analyses are also relocated and regrouped.

improvement.justification: The broader evaluation, explicit retrieval controls, and expanded reproduction guidance improve assessment of SWAT's applicability and failure conditions. These gains are tempered by removal of the same-data WiSE-FT/FLYP comparison and overstatements in new analyses: v2 Table 9 claims filtering outperforms CLAP, although 4-shot Cars remains lower at 83.5 versus 84.9. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
